metadata.title: Claude, Claim Chart.
metadata.purpose: Answer what a finished claim chart actually proves: is a chart with every cell filled in the strong version of it? Lands the carry-out that the chart's job is a pin cite for what's supported and a flag, element by element, for what's missing.
metadata.source_note: Unlike sibling redos in this family (amendment-history, ai-inventory), the source sheet's narration carried REAL facts, not unfilled placeholders: claim-chart builds/reviews an element chart (patent claim chart or civil element chart), every cell pin-cited, gap detection as the priority output. See QUESTION.md.

beats.narration_text: Someone building a claim chart assumes a filled cell means proof. It doesn't -- the real value is which cells can't be filled. The real question: where does the evidence actually run out, element by element?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Can Claude prove my case with a claim chart?', hesitates on 'prove', corrects to 'map', lands the real question

props.text:

my case with

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('prove' -> 'map') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: A legal claim breaks into separate elements, and each one needs its own proof. Build the chart, and the easy move is to treat a full grid as a strong case -- every box has an entry, so every element must be covered. But a filled cell only shows a citation was found. It says nothing about whether that citation actually proves the element.

shot.new_visual_element: A chart grid filling in, cell by cell, each one glowing 'covered' as it fills

production_viz.label: A full grid reads as a strong case
production_viz.mechanic: A claim chart grid: rows are elements, one column. Cells fill left to right, each landing with a soft 'COVERED' stamp. The whole grid fills, looking complete. A caption fades in beneath: 'a filled cell only shows a citation was found.'

beats.narration_text: A claim chart works element by element: for every element, it finds the passage that could support it and pin-cites the exact page and line. Watch two elements from the same claim: 'a locking mechanism' turns up a citation straight to the product manual, page twelve. 'A temperature sensor' turns up nothing in the same manual -- no citation exists to put in that cell.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- two element rows on one chart: one cell fills with a pin cite, the other stays empty, flagged

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one cited, one gapped
production_viz.mechanic: Two rows of one chart: 'A LOCKING MECHANISM' fills with 'MANUAL, P.12' pin-cited beneath it. 'A TEMPERATURE SENSOR' stays empty, then a terracotta 'GAP' tag drops in beneath it. THIS EXACT TWO-ROW CHART RETURNS, RESOLVED, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: So on this chart, the locking-mechanism cell reads 'supported -- manual, page twelve,' and the temperature-sensor cell reads 'no citation found' -- a gap, flagged on purpose. A filled cell doesn't decide the case: a citation can be weak, or cover only part of the element. And a gap doesn't decide it either -- it isn't proof the element fails, only proof no evidence has turned up yet. Either way, the chart shows exactly where to look next.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the two rows resolve, then split into 'filled != proven' and 'gap != failed'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- filled != proven, gap != failed
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 TWO-ROW CHART RETURNS, identical placement, both cells now settled: locking-mechanism cell reads 'SUPPORTED -- MANUAL, P.12', temperature-sensor cell reads 'NO CITATION FOUND' under its GAP tag. It then splits into two cards: left reads 'a citation can be weak or partial' beneath 'FILLED != PROVEN'; right reads 'no evidence found YET' beneath 'GAP != FAILED', connected only by a dashed line labelled 'shows where to look next'.

beats.narration_text: The point of a claim chart isn't a full grid -- it's a pin cite for what's supported, and a flag, element by element, for what's missing.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. Paste in the claim language, element by element, along with the accused product's documentation. Then ask: for each element, find the exact passage that supports it, cite it, and flag any element with no citation as a gap -- don't guess to fill it in. Liam, in for Bear.
